issues.legal_issue: A remarriage contracted within the restricted period after a divorce decree is not void solely because it violates the statutory waiting-period restriction, and the remarried person retains spousal status and the resulting claim to inherit.
material_facts: The deceased’s earlier marriage had been dissolved by a divorce decree.
The deceased contracted a second marriage before one year had elapsed from the date of the divorce decree in the court of first instance.
After the deceased died, relatives challenged the second spouse’s claim as widow and heir solely on the ground that the second marriage violated the waiting-period restriction.
issues.conclusion: The second marriage was not void merely because it contravened the waiting-period restriction. The appellant retained the status of wife and widow and could claim as an heir.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 5 and 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, only marriages breaching the specified conditions are expressly made void; section 18 penalizes breaches of specified conditions but not the waiting-period restriction. The statutory scheme therefore does not support inferring that a marriage violating that restriction is void, particularly when the restriction supplies no stated consequence for breach. The Court also considered section 16, the regulatory purpose of the restriction, and its later deletion by the Marriage Laws (Amendment) Act, 1976. Chandra Mohini Srivastava v. Avinash Prasad Srivastava and Marsh v. Marsh were referred to; Muhammad Hayat v. Muhammad Nawaz was followed on the treatment of marriage during iddat. The Court distinguished decisions under section 57 of the Indian Divorce Act, including Warter v. Warter, J. S. Battie v. G. E. Brown, Turner v. Turner and Jackson v. Jackson, and disapproved Uma Charan Roy v. Smt. Kajal Roy.

rule.if: appeal_from_denial_of_widow_heir_status and prior_marriage_dissolved_by_divorce and remarriage_before_waiting_period_elapsed and remarriage_otherwise_valid and law_does_not_specify_nullity_or_penalty_for_breach

predicates.appeal_from_denial_of_widow_heir_status: A person appeals after a court denies claimed widow or heir status on the ground that a remarriage was void.
predicates.prior_marriage_dissolved_by_divorce: A person’s earlier marriage was dissolved by a divorce decree.
predicates.remarriage_before_waiting_period_elapsed: The person remarried before the applicable post-divorce waiting period had elapsed.
predicates.remarriage_otherwise_valid: The remarriage satisfied the other applicable conditions for a valid marriage.
predicates.law_does_not_specify_nullity_or_penalty_: The governing law neither declares a marriage void nor prescribes a penalty for breaching the waiting-period restriction.

issues.definition: When a person appeals the denial of widow or heir status after remarrying within the post-divorce waiting period, and the remarriage otherwise satisfies the applicable validity conditions while the law specifies no nullity or penalty for the breach, the marriage is not void and spousal status is retained.
